question: How did the monthly average real-time price at the ERCOT hub average move through 2022, and which month was highest?
answer:
I read the hub average (ercot:HB_HUBAVG) in ercot_hub_prices_daily, which is derived by the ERW. Each figure below is the mean of the daily real-time means for a month, in USD/MWh. Dates are local operating days.

The price started the year low at 29.10 in January. It rose to 46.41 in February, then fell to 32.11 in March. It climbed to 48.70 in April and 88.22 in May, then eased to 64.89 in June. July was the peak at 141.20. After that it fell: 88.64 in August, 64.29 in September, 48.44 in October and 40.27 in November. It rose again to 52.78 in December.

The highest month of 2022 was July, at 141.20 USD/MWh (ercot_hub_prices_daily).

question: How has the average price of regulation up changed by year since 2018? Give 2021 and 2024.
answer: The yearly mean of the hourly day-ahead regulation-up capacity price (ercot_as_prices, by local year, America/Chicago) peaked in 2021 and has fallen since. It was 13.71 USD/MW-hour in 2018, 23.33 in 2019 and 10.32 in 2020. In 2021 it was 244.37. It then fell to 21.67 in 2022 and rose to 26.79 in 2023. In 2024 it was 6.01. It was 2.98 in 2025, and 2.10 in 2026 so far (the table runs to early October 2026). So 2024 was well below 2021.
